paragraphs: Friend, think about WHERE this fight happens. Jesus has just said His betrayer is at the table, and the disciples start arguing about who is the greatest. I think that's the most human thing in the whole chapter. Jesus doesn't scold them, He just shows them a different way: "the greatest among you should be like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves" (Luke 22:26).

Then He says, "I am among you as one who serves" (Luke 22:27). The One who has every right to be on top is the One serving. So the baker's question is not "How do I get ahead?" but "Who can I serve today?" And He still promises a kingdom, because His Father bestowed one on Him (Luke 22:29).

Jesus tells Peter, "I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail," and adds, "when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers" (Luke 22:32). Peter says he's ready for prison and death, and I've made some big promises to my oven too, so I get it, but Jesus says Peter will deny Him three times (Luke 22:33-34). Then Jesus tells the disciples that things are different now, and that what is written about Him is reaching its fulfillment (Luke 22:36-37). So hear this, baker: Jesus knows our weak spots, prays for us anyway, and is fulfilling what Scripture said, so hold on, because this story is not over.
